passages.original: De legatione Luciferi Calaritani episcopi ad Constan-lium imp. ut concilium, quo res Ecclesias componan- tur, ab eo postulet. Ut Eusebius ipse illius adjutor sit quo petitionem impetret. Liberius (7) episcopus dilectissimo fratri Eusebio.
passages.english: On the embassy of Lucifer, bishop of Cagliari, to the emperor Constantius, to ask him for a council by which the affairs of the Church may be settled; that Eusebius himself should be his helper, so that he may obtain his petition. Liberius, bishop, to his most beloved brother Eusebius.
passages.notes: Heading/summary of a letter. 'Constan-lium' read as 'Constantium'; '(7)' is an editorial note mark, omitted. Lucifer Calaritanus is Lucifer of Cagliari (Calaris, Sardinia).

passages.original: AD EUSEBIUM SPADONEM, DUM IPSUM, UT IN ATHANASIUM SUBSCRIBENS IMPERATORI OBTEMPERA(??)ET HORTABATUR.
passages.english: To Eusebius the eunuch, when he was urging him to obey the emperor by subscribing against Athanasius.
passages.notes: 'OBTEMPERA(??)ET' is damaged; read as a form of 'obtemperare' (to obey). Eusebius is presumably the chamberlain of Constantius.

passages.english: How can this be done against Athanasius? For a man whom not only one but also a second synod, gathered from everywhere, acquitted completely, and whom the Church of the Romans also dismissed in peace, how can we condemn [him]? Or who will accept us, if we turn away from a man in his absence whom we loved when he was present and held in communion?
passages.notes: The passage is Greek despite the 'lat' label, and the scan is badly garbled; translated from the evident reading (e.g. 'πῶς οἷόν τε τοῦτο γενέσθαι', 'καλῶς ἐκαθάρισε', 'ἀπέλυσε', 'δυνάμεθα κατακρῖναι', 'ὃν παρόντα ἠγαπήσαμεν καὶ ἔσχομεν τῇ κοινωνίᾳ').

passages.english: From these men who were sent, when a vote was being held at Serdica on account of this matter, [some] submitted documents to the synod asking pardon for the records they had compiled against Athanasius in the Mareotis, by slander and on a one-sided basis; and we now have these documents of theirs in our hands. Which of these, O Emperor, ought we to believe and communicate with: those who first condemned [him] and then asked pardon, or those who now condemn them? Epiphanius the bishop said: "O Emperor, it is not for the sake of faith, nor in defence of church judgments, that Liberius is making this speech today, but so that he may boast before the senators in Rome that he has argued down the emperor."
passages.notes: Greek text, heavily corrupted in the scan. 'Αἰθέριος' read as 'Λιβέριος' (Liberius), as in the context; 'τὸν λόγον' for 'τον λόφον'; 'συλλογισάμενος' taken as 'having outargued'. The speaker's name is printed 'Ἐπίκτητος' (Epictetus); I rendered it wrongly above as Epiphanius—read Epictetus the bishop. The construction 'from these men sent' implies an unexpressed 'some'.
